answer: Each identity claims a dune crest plot, posts a 70-credit bond, and files weight and ferrous fraction from a marked point. A raven witness timestamps the sampling and files the code. An auditor recomputes the fraction against a public dune assay table, burning the bond on a deviation over 3% or a reused code. First assay costs 33; the kth costs 33+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6027 and 1000 fakes pay 3,030,000 plus 70,000 locked bonds. A rented-sample ring fails: one sample cannot assay two plots and reuse burns both bonds; honest samplers pay 33 once and recover it on a clean audit.
